ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is glass rod S1, whose right end is a convex curved surface; on the right side is glass rod S2, whose left end is a convex curved surface. The dashed axes of the two rods are collinear, and there is a point light source P on the axis inside S1, labeled with its distance to the vertex of the curved surface of S1 as 50 cm; the distance between the vertices of the two curved surfaces is labeled d. Reasoning: Take the vertex of the curved surface of S1 as x=0, with rightward as positive. The spherical refraction formula is n2/v - n1/u = (n2-n1)/R. The first surface is from glass to air, n1=1.5, n2=1, u=-50 cm; the center of curvature of the convex surface at the right end of S1 is on the left side, so R1=-10 cm. Substituting gives 1/v - 1.5/(-50) = (1-1.5)/(-10), that is, 1/v + 0.03 = 0.05, so v=50 cm. Therefore S1 alone would form an intermediate real image 50 cm to the right of its curved surface. The second surface is from air to glass, and it is required that the light rays after entering S2 be parallel, so v=∞. The center of curvature of the convex surface at the left end of S2 is on the right side, so R2=+10 cm. Substituting 0 - 1/u = (1.5-1)/10 = 0.05 gives u=-20 cm. Therefore the intermediate image must be located 20 cm to the left of the curved surface of S2. Thus the distance between the vertices of the two curved surfaces is d = 50 + 20 = 70 cm.

From the image, take S1 on the left with its convex curved end facing right toward the gap, and S2 on the right with its convex curved end facing left; the dashed horizontal line is the common axis, and d is the axial separation between the two curved vertices. From the text, use n_glass=1.5, n_air=1, |R|=10 cm, and P is 50 cm to the left of S1's curved face. Set the first vertex as x=0 and positive direction left-to-right. For the first surface, glass to air, u=-50 cm and R1=-10 cm, so use n2/v - n1/u = (n2-n1)/R: 1/v - 1.5/(-50) = (1-1.5)/(-10), giving v=50 cm in the air gap. Thus S1 alone would form a real image 50 cm to the right of its curved surface. For the second surface to make rays parallel inside S2, set v=infinity for air to glass at the left convex face of S2; from the image its centre of curvature is to the right, so R2=+10 cm. Then 0 - 1/u = (1.5-1)/10, so u=-20 cm. Hence the object for S2 must be 20 cm to its left. Therefore S2's surface must be 20 cm to the right of the intermediate image: d=50+20=70 cm.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Two identical glass rods $S_1$ and $S_2$ (refractive index = 1.5) have one convex end of radius of curvature 10 cm. They are placed with the curved surfaces at a distance $d$ as shown in the figure, with their axes (shown by the dashed line) aligned. When a point source of light $P$ is placed inside rod $S_1$ on its axis at a distance of 50 cm from the curved face, the light rays emanating from it are found to be parallel to the axis inside $S_2$. What is the distance $d$?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is glass rod S1, whose right end is a convex curved surface; on the right side is glass rod S2, whose left end is a convex curved surface. The dashed axes of the two rods are collinear, and there is a point light source P on the axis inside S1, labeled with its distance to the vertex of the curved surface of S1 as 50 cm; the distance between the vertices of the two curved surfaces is labeled d. Reasoning: Take the vertex of the curved surface of S1 as x=0, with rightward as positive. The spherical refraction formula is n2/v - n1/u = (n2-n1)/R. The first surface is from glass to air, n1=1.5, n2=1, u=-50 cm; the center of curvature of the convex surface at the right end of S1 is on the left side, so R1=-10 cm. Substituting gives 1/v - 1.5/(-50) = (1-1.5)/(-10), that is, 1/v + 0.03 = 0.05, so v=50 cm. Therefore S1 alone would form an intermediate real image 50 cm to the right of its curved surface. The second surface is from air to glass, and it is required that the light rays after entering S2 be parallel, so v=∞. The center of curvature of the convex surface at the left end of S2 is on the right side, so R2=+10 cm. Substituting 0 - 1/u = (1.5-1)/10 = 0.05 gives u=-20 cm. Therefore the intermediate image must be located 20 cm to the left of the curved surface of S2. Thus the distance between the vertices of the two curved surfaces is d = 50 + 20 = 70 cm.
